name: Grapevine
summary: Shopify-native survey platform for post-purchase, NPS, CSAT and attribution questions, with unlimited responses on a single plan. Reports revenue and AOV per marketing channel, targets surveys by order value, product, country, payment method or customer, runs on-site, by email and on Shopify POS, and exports to Shopify Flow, Klaviyo and GA4; survey data can be queried with your own AI assistant through the vendor's MCP server. Launched August 2017.
best_for: Shopify stores running more than one marketing channel that want attribution from customers rather than from cookies: post-purchase 'how did you hear about us', NPS and CSAT: with unlimited responses at a predictable flat price, and that already send data into Klaviyo, GA4 or Shopify Flow
skip_if: your order volume is small enough that $25 a month buys a handful of answers; you want a single one-off survey rather than a running programme; or you need a permanently free tier, because the only free access here is the 14-day trial
honest_knock: The flat price is the whole pricing page, which cuts both ways. There is no free tier and no small plan, so from day fifteen the app costs $25 a month whether it collects four responses or forty thousand: a low-volume store pays the same as a high-volume one, and several of the nearest alternatives do publish a free plan. The second thing to weigh is access rather than price: the listing's data section asks for customer data including sensitive, device and activity data, plus orders, staff accounts and the online store, which is a lot of reach for a survey tool and worth reading the privacy policy over. The evidence base is otherwise good for a Shopify app: launched 17 August 2017 by Union Works Apps in London, and 232 reviews on 13 October 2026 of which 225 are five-star and none below four.

pricing.notes: (read 2026-09-10 on apps.shopify.com/grapevine) One plan, called Complete, at $25 a month, billed in USD every 30 days, with a 14-day free trial and no free tier. There is no response limit and no per-response charge: unlimited post-purchase, NPS, CSAT and attribution responses are included at that price, on every Shopify plan. The single price also covers revenue and AOV reporting per marketing channel, targeting by order value, product, country, payment method and customer, delivery on-site, by email and on Shopify POS, exports to Shopify Flow, Klaviyo and GA4, and querying your survey data with your own AI assistant through the vendor's MCP server.

schema_offer.description: Complete, per month, billed month-to-month. From our pricing notes: “One plan, called Complete, at $25 a month, billed in USD every 30 days, with a 14-day free trial and no free tier” Read on the vendor's own pricing page on 2026-11-01.

compare_with.name: Zigpoll Customer Surveys, Fairing Post Purchase Surveys
compare_with.why: all three do post-purchase and attribution surveys, and the honest split is volume against entry price. Zigpoll and Fairing both advertise a free plan on their listings (read 10 September 2026), so a store sending a few dozen surveys a month can start at nothing; Grapevine has no free tier and asks $25 from the end of the trial. What Grapevine buys for that is the absence of a response meter, the plan states unlimited responses with no extra charge, plus revenue and AOV per channel and an MCP endpoint so you can interrogate the answers with your own AI assistant. Check the response limits on the free plans before you assume they are cheaper for you: a free plan that caps at a few hundred responses is a different product from an uncapped one.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Grapevine Surveys on a Shopify development store: the install, the Shopify test charge (approved without a card, billed 0 dollars), the Setup Assistant, an attribution survey from a template, the survey page with zero impressions, the plan page and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. No checkout block was added and no order was placed. Install: the App Store listing (English) is called Grapevine Surveys, from Union Works Apps, and says $25/month. Free trial available., with a rating of 5.0 from 243 reviews (the dossier had 232 reviews on 13 October). Install was clicked at about 11:58; the Install app dialog asked for View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data. The Install button on the listing is a form that opens a new tab; we sent it in our own tab instead. Right after the install the Shopify Approve subscription screen came up, and after approval the app opened (Welcome to Grapevine Surveys, Setup Assistant) at about 11:59. Core action: the Setup Assistant asked What is your main goal? (we chose Understand where customers come from), Where do you want to survey customers? (Post purchase pages) and recommended the Acquisition Insight Survey with 4 questions included. After Use this template the editor said Template loaded and preloaded the questions and channels: 1 How did you first hear about us? with Social Media, Search Engine, AI Recommendation, YouTube, Influencer, Friend or Family, Podcast and Other; 2 What made you decide to buy from us today?; 3 How would you rate your website experience today?; 4 What could we improve about your website experience? The channel is Checkout app block and the display rule is The customer is new. Save gave Survey Saved. The survey page then showed Total impressions 0, Responses 0 and Response rate 0%, and Setup instructions: Make sure you have added the Grapevine checkout block to your thank you and order status pages. So the survey only appears after the checkout app block is added by hand in the checkout editor. We did NOT do that, so nothing was changed in the theme or the checkout, no test order was placed and no answer or attribution data exists. The preview in the editor showed a thank you page for an example name from the app. Timing, approximate tester observations: about 2 minutes from the install click (11:58) to the saved survey (about 12:00), in 6 steps after the approval (3 assistant clicks, the template, Ok, Save). Checkout: the Approve subscription screen shows the plan Complete at $25,00 USD every 30 days, You will not be billed for this test charge., You have a 14-day free trial ending on 1 Dec., a subtotal of $25,00 plus any applicable taxes and a total of $25,00 due 1 Dec. An Add payment method row was visible but no card was needed; we approved this test charge, which cost nothing. The price matches the listing. Plan: the Your Plan page shows only one plan, Complete Plan at $25 /month, with Unlimited responses, Revenue reports, Klaviyo integration, Google Analytics integration, POS surveys and more; there is no free tier. Cancelling: Settings, Apps, Uninstall opens the dialog Uninstall Grapevine Surveys? with the notes that data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted and that a request goes to the developer within 48 hours to delete personal customer information. A Reason for uninstalling is required: the Uninstall button stays grey until a reason is chosen (we chose Testing multiple apps). Not tested: adding the checkout app block and placing a test order (so no real answer and no channel report), Klaviyo, GA4, MCP, one-click email surveys, POS, translation, changing the Display Rules, and the Book a call and Chat with us options. Clean up: the app was uninstalled after the test and Shopify confirmed it; the saved survey went with it. No theme or checkout change was made and the test charge ended with the app. Our own tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The saved survey does not show to buyers until the checkout app block is added by hand in the checkout editor, and the app has one paid plan and no free tier.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Grapevine Surveys on a Shopify development store: the install, the Shopify test charge (approved without a card, billed 0 dollars), the Setup Assistant, an attribution survey from a template, the survey page with zero impressions, the plan page and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. No checkout block was added and no order was placed. Install: the App Store listing (English) is called Grapevine Surveys, from Union Works Apps, and says $25/month. Free trial available., with a rating of 5.0 from 243 reviews (the dossier had 232 reviews on 13 October). Install was clicked at about 11:58; the Install app dialog asked for View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data. The Install button on the listing is a form that opens a new tab; we sent it in our own tab instead. Right after the install the Shopify Approve subscription screen came up, and after approval the app opened (Welcome to Grapevine Surveys, Setup Assistant) at about 11:59. Core action: the Setup Assistant asked What is your main goal? (we chose Understand where customers come from), Where do you want to survey customers? (Post purchase pages) and recommended the Acquisition Insight Survey with 4 questions included. After Use this template the editor said Template loaded and preloaded the questions and channels: 1 How did you first hear about us? with Social Media, Search Engine, AI Recommendation, YouTube, Influencer, Friend or Family, Podcast and Other; 2 What made you decide to buy from us today?; 3 How would you rate your website experience today?; 4 What could we improve about your website experience? The channel is Checkout app block and the display rule is The customer is new. Save gave Survey Saved. The survey page then showed Total impressions 0, Responses 0 and Response rate 0%, and Setup instructions: Make sure you have added the Grapevine checkout block to your thank you and order status pages. So the survey only appears after the checkout app block is added by hand in the checkout editor. We did NOT do that, so nothing was changed in the theme or the checkout, no test order was placed and no answer or attribution data exists. The preview in the editor showed a thank you page for an example name from the app. Timing, approximate tester observations: about 2 minutes from the install click (11:58) to the saved survey (about 12:00), in 6 steps after the approval (3 assistant clicks, the template, Ok, Save). Checkout: the Approve subscription screen shows the plan Complete at $25,00 USD every 30 days, You will not be billed for this test charge., You have a 14-day free trial ending on 1 Dec., a subtotal of $25,00 plus any applicable taxes and a total of $25,00 due 1 Dec. An Add payment method row was visible but no card was needed; we approved this test charge, which cost nothing. The price matches the listing. Plan: the Your Plan page shows only one plan, Complete Plan at $25 /month, with Unlimited responses, Revenue reports, Klaviyo integration, Google Analytics integration, POS surveys and more; there is no free tier. Cancelling: Settings, Apps, Uninstall opens the dialog Uninstall Grapevine Surveys? with the notes that data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted and that a request goes to the developer within 48 hours to delete personal customer information. A Reason for uninstalling is required: the Uninstall button stays grey until a reason is chosen (we chose Testing multiple apps). Not tested: adding the checkout app block and placing a test order (so no real answer and no channel report), Klaviyo, GA4, MCP, one-click email surveys, POS, translation, changing the Display Rules, and the Book a call and Chat with us options. Clean up: the app was uninstalled after the test and Shopify confirmed it; the saved survey went with it. No theme or checkout change was made and the test charge ended with the app. Our own tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The saved survey does not show to buyers until the checkout app block is added by hand in the checkout editor, and the app has one paid plan and no free tier.
